The converter’s push-mode VTN then wrote the new report to a stack of reports. The converter’s pull-mode VEN then frequently checked the stack for new reports and repackaged the reports and sent them to the pull-mode VTN. The pull-push converter had been tested successfully, demonstrating that it can register reports received from the push-VEN with the pull-VTN, send new report update messages between those two devices, and send events from the pull-VTN to the push-VEN. In order to send telemetry reports from USU’s microgrid VEN to RMP’s VTN and to send events in the opposite direction, firewall changes were made at both PAC and USU to allow the other to send web traffic through the enterprise firewalls. The OpenADR connection between USU and RMP was successfully tested in August 2025, with the USU VEN able to register itself with the RMP VTN, send reports to the RMP VTN, and receive events pushed by the RMP VTN. 18 The OpenADR VEN at USU’s microgrid received events and sent reports. Events were executed by using a number of Python handlers, each of which communicate with a different DER. USU developed an API which allowed the handlers to write the important event details including the magnitude and timing of the events, which were then executed on the DERs themselves. These APIs were housed in the ASPIRE Tool Suite (ATS), as depicted below. 6.1.8.1.2 Microgrid Communications Figure 2: USU Microgrid and EVR Architecture Diagram The ASPIRE software stack was built around secure, scalable communication between DERs. At the USU EVR and microgrid facility, this was accomplished through a structured API framework that routes semantic requests across heterogeneous equipment management servers, another capability of the ATS. All devices were registered in a centralized database prior to use, enabling the system to identify the equipment by type and ID, translate the request into the appropriate protocol, and forward it to the correct service. 19 For the current deployment, EV chargers were managed through an OCPP 1.6 server, which authenticated incoming commands and directed them to the designated charger by ID. Renewable generation, and energy storage assets were coordinated through OpenADR: solar and battery commands were routed to a VTN, which relayed them securely to a VEN operating within the system. This distributed architecture not only ensured robust interoperability across device classes but also provided a foundation for rapid scaling to additional equipment while maintaining high levels of security and reliability. 6.1.8.1.3 DERMS System Configuration and Software Installation Figure 3: USU Microgrid Facility Controls and EVSE Dashboard In preparation for the full execution of DER control in the UDERMS project, PacifiCorp and OSI installed and configured the OSI Monarch system along with the DERMS applications: integraDERMS and DERComms. • IntegraDERMS is the core DERMS application that is installed on a dedicated server that is responsible for all the main core DER functions like estimation, optimization and scheduling. • DERComms is an
